_comment: EXAMPLE · TABLEFRAME OPERATIONS — the transforms a @transformer is made of, over three seeded tables (customers, a customers_previous snapshot, orders) so joins and diffs have something real to work on. USE THE TABLEFRAME API, NOT POLARS: a TableFrame carries the framework's system columns alongside the data and the TableFrame operations maintain them; _to_polars_lf() loses that bookkeeping, so it belongs at the edges only. ROW-PRESERVING (select / filter / join / sort / rename / with_columns / head) vs RESHAPING (group_by().agg(), which builds new rows) is the distinction that matters at a SINK — aggregate freely mid-pipeline, keep the last hop before a destination row-preserving. FOUR FAMILIES, one function per file: JOIN (join_inner, join_left — customer 5 has no orders — join_composite_key, plus the country_right collision and the fan-out a too-narrow key causes); DIFF (there is no .diff() — a row-level difference IS a join: how="anti" for rows with NO match gives arrived/left, how="semi" for rows WITH one gives the intersection, and neither adds the right side's columns nor can fan out); PROJECTION (project_columns for select/rename/sort — project early, it is the cheapest optimisation there is — and project_derived for with_columns/filter/lit); AGGREGATION (agg_by_country for the reductions and aliases, agg_top_customers for the real shape: aggregate, join back to a dimension for labels, sort, head(N) — in that order, so the join runs on the reduced frame), plus union_and_dedupe for concat vertical-vs-diagonal and unique(subset=...). Input refs show the @NEW / @HEAD split: @NEW on the driving table, @HEAD on the lookup. Dev-only: this suite needs no external backend. Run: `tdx-xp oneshot --suite examples/tableframe_ops`.
